column1: # Everything billet's guest build does differently from GitHub's template, in one
# place. One entry per line, tab-separated: action, step id (from plan.json), reason.
#   skip           the step does not run; the runner says so when it reaches it
#   prepare:<name> the runner's prepare_<name> runs in the target just before the step
# A step id that is not in the plan, or a prepare the runner does not implement,
# stops the build before anything runs: an entry that no longer names anything is
# a pin bump to review, not a line to ignore.

column3: Azure's agent deprovisions the VM for capture; a billet guest is not an Azure VM and carries no waagent

Ubuntu's generic cloud image has no /etc/waagent.conf, and the script edits it unconditionally under bash -e; an empty file lets the rest of the script run, and the Azure resource-disk settings it writes are read by nothing

billet's /var/lib/docker is one independently fenced cache filesystem, so docker must keep images in its classic overlay2 store rather than Docker 29's containerd store, which keeps content outside it; written before the script first starts dockerd and pulls into it

the script restarts snapd, which needs AppArmor profiles and squashfs mounts a container build does not give it, and a billet guest runs no snaps; /snap/bin on PATH and the refresh hold describe a snapd that is not running
GitHub runs this step as Packer's unprivileged SSH user, because Homebrew refuses to install as root; billet runs it as runner, created here with GitHub's uid and passwordless sudo

the script writes the root filesystem's ext4 options as a GRUB drop-in and runs update-grub under bash -e; Ubuntu's cloud root filesystem has no GRUB and a Firecracker guest's kernel is booted directly, so a stand-in answers that one call and removes itself; the drop-in ships and nothing reads it

GitHub's system tests assert an sd* or nvme* block device with the read-ahead its udev rule sets, which is Azure's disk; a Firecracker guest's disks are virtio, so that one assertion is marked -Skip and the rest of the suite still runs

two system tests assert the relaxed ext4 options GRUB puts on Azure's kernel command line and the root filesystem mounted with them; the build's container sees the builder's command line and mount, and a billet guest is not booted through GRUB, so those two are marked -Skip and the drop-in's own test still runs

the apt test that the sources resolve through GitHub's mirror list is marked -Skip: billet's source names two HTTPS mirrors as two repositories, which kept apt working with the first black-holed where a mirror list did not (measured 2026-09-11); the mirror list itself and GitHub's acquire settings are still tested
